rule: Any joint rated >= 4 (1-5) makes the day Red and pulls a deload forward immediately
summary: A 4/5 joint rating is near the magnitude of a self-reported flare (Suri 2025: ~2.8 NRS points above baseline) and fits the consensus definition of a flare that impacts usual activity. Acting on it the same day is conservative; the separate red-flag pathway (sharp/worsening pain, radiating symptoms) still sends the athlete to a doctor, consistent with IFOMPT's emphasis on clinical reasoning and referral. Unvalidated number but cheap relative to training on a flaring joint.

sources.note: Self-reported LBP flare associated with ~2.8 NRS points higher pain, more interference and analgesic use (11,817 surveys)
Delphi LBP flare definition: a worsening lasting hours to weeks, hard to tolerate, impacting usual activities
IFOMPT red-flag framework: red flags have poor accuracy alone; clinical reasoning and onward referral when suspicion rises
OSTRC weekly questionnaire (knee/low back/shoulder): repeated self-report captures far more overuse problems than time-loss reporting
